name: Sumi-e Ink
summary: Monochrome ink-wash painting in motion: black sumi in five tones on warm xuan paper, one-stroke brushwork, lots of empty space, one vermilion accent.
description: Everything is painted with one black ink diluted into five tones, from burnt black to a clear grey wash, on warm rice paper with visible fibres. Every figure is a handful of confident strokes with pressed starts, tapering ends and dry-brush streaks: a wandering calligrapher under a wide sedge hat with a vermilion sash, a hopping crow, a scuttling crab, a pale carp that swims through the air and a striped tiger. Most of the sheet stays empty: pale hill washes with one hard dried edge, ponds and streams left as bare paper inside their banks, swept footpaths, bamboo groves, plum trees leaning over the water and homesteads with stone lanterns. The only colour is vermilion, kept for seals, blossoms and the sash.
bestFor: calm exploration and travel games with an East-Asian theme
martial-arts and folklore action games that want a painterly look
story maps, title screens and scroll-based menus
avoidFor: projects that need colour coding by hue
neon, sci-fi or gritty modern settings
very dense screens where empty space cannot survive

difficulty.why: New assets are quick to sketch with the brush() and wash() toolkit and need no colour design, but they only read when the strokes are few and placed with intent: choosing the five to twelve strokes that carry a figure, giving every animal a drawn cycle of 4-8 poses, balancing the five ink tones for depth and keeping most of the paper empty is the real craft.

technique.resolution: Native resolution, smooth scaling. Characters baked at 5 px per world unit, props at 3 px, small effect sprites at 5-12 px; ground chunks of 256 units rendered per pixel at up to 2.5 px per unit.
technique.summary: Every mark is a filled brush ribbon along a Catmull-Rom spline whose width follows a pressed start, a wobble and a tapering end; dry strokes switch to 4-18 parallel bristle ribbons that end early and break into gaps along 1D noise (flying white). Washes are filled shapes with blurred darker and lighter blots, a dried rim, granulation and an optional bleed halo. Each figure is painted once per pose from a pose record (body drop, lean, arm swing, leg positions, lag of hat and brush) and baked; a fibre pattern is cut out of every sprite so the ink sits in the paper.
technique.linework: No closed outlines: contours are brush strokes that are pressed at one end and run dry at the other. Main character: back stroke of the robe 3.0 units (burnt black to dan, dry 0.6), front contour 1.4, sleeve 2.2, hat brim 1.5 (pressed at the back, dry at the front), hem 1.05, folds 0.75-0.95, face line 0.48. Crow wing 3.3 units, beak 1.55; tiger stripes 1.1-2.3 units pressed at the spine; prop strokes 0.4-5.2 units (plum trunk 5.2, pine trunk 4.4). Width = w * (0.3 + 0.7 sqrt(u / ta)) at the start, * (0.04 + 0.96 ((1 - u) / tb)^0.6) at the end, * (1 + press * exp(-s^2 / 1.2 w^2)) at a pressed head, * (1 + 0.12 wobble).
technique.shading: Value only, from the five ink tones: dark wet blots inside washes (blurred 0.5-2 units), bare-paper belly patches, a dried darker rim along wash edges and the tip-to-belly ink mix across dry bristles. Depth by value: the far leg, far wing, far legs of the tiger and back bamboo stalks are one tone paler than the near ones.
technique.lighting: No light source and no highlights except bare-paper glints. Readability comes from value: the crow and crab are the darkest masses, the carp and tiger are pale washes held by black strokes, the main character is a pale robe framed by a black hat brim and back stroke plus the only vermilion. Shadows are soft pale ink ellipses rgba(58,54,48,.34 -> 0).
technique.texture: Warm xuan paper: a 512 px fibre tile (2600 curved hairs, 62 % light), 256 px paper tooth noise, a granulation tile multiplied into every wash at 0.3-0.8, and a light-fibre pattern cut out of every sprite with destination-out at 0.28 (characters) / 0.35 (props).

palette.name: Xuan paper
palette.role: The sheet: ground base (~75 % of the screen), panel paper, misty margin

palette.name: Unpainted paper
palette.role: Brightest paper: faces, eyes, bellies, mist bands, the hit flash (ink lifted)

palette.name: Jiao (burnt ink)
palette.role: Darkest tone: crow, crab shell, hat brim, tiger stripes, moss dots, text

palette.name: Nong (thick ink)
palette.role: Bold contours, bamboo stalks, shore strokes, grass, HUD bar fill

palette.name: Zhong (heavy ink)
palette.role: Mid tone: inner blots, ripples, far legs, pine trunks, card text

palette.name: Dan (light ink)
palette.role: Robe and body shading, hat wash, path edges, wakes, far props

palette.name: Qing (clear ink)
palette.role: Pale washes: robe, carp and tiger bodies, mist trail, far peaks, bar tracks

palette.name: Ground ink
palette.role: Ink mixed into the paper by the ground shader (wash density 0.02-0.2)

palette.name: Vermilion
palette.role: The only colour: seals, plum blossoms and petals, the sash, orbit dots, card keys

palette.name: Vermilion deep
palette.role: The far sash tail, caption text; blossom centres and sash shading use #a02618

palette.name: Silk mounting

paletteRules: Monochrome first: every mark uses one of the five ink tones over warm paper; tones are mixed by alpha and across the bristles of a dry stroke, never by hue.
Vermilion appears only as seals, plum blossoms and petals, the main character's sash, the dots inside the orbiting circles and card keys; keep it under about 2 % of the screen.
No pure black and no pure white: the darkest ink is #161412, the brightest paper #f9f4e8.
Leave most of the sheet empty paper (ma); ground washes stay under 20 % density and decals gather at features.
Value carries depth: far parts pale (dan / qing), near parts dark (nong / jiao).
Water is never painted: it is bare paper framed by bank washes, broken shore strokes and a few ripple lines.

typography.role: Titles, clock, counters, floating numbers, seal numerals

typography.role: Captions, labels, hints (grass-script feel), often in vermilion
typography.css: font: 400 19px/1.1 'Zhi Mang Xing', 'Ma Shan Zheng', cursive; color: #ce3c26;

typography.css: font: italic 600 18px/1.2 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif; color: #56524c;

world.summary: An endless sheet of xuan paper painted per pixel in 256-unit chunks and composed from four signed-distance fields: pale hill washes with one hard dried upper edge and a long soft fade below, ponds and thin streams left as bare paper inside darker banks, and winding footpaths swept clean of ink. Brush marks gather only at those features, so the open paper stays empty. Chunks are built by a generator in small time slices.
layers: Paper: #f3ecdd * (0.966 + 0.05 tooth + 0.12 fibres), a few faint foxing spots; fibres are a 512 px tile of curved hairs

Hill washes (domain-warped fbm, scale 500, threshold 0.615): the edge whose wash lies below it is hard and dried (rim +0.07), the other edges soften over up to 19 units into mist; density 0.022 + 0.1 * exp(-d / 9..33), granulated

Water: ponds (warped fbm, scale 820, threshold 0.625) and streams (zero line of warped noise at scale 860, half width 5.5-10.5, masked so they thin out) are bare paper, a faint shore wash inside, a bank wash outside that is darkest at the water and fades over 8-24 units
Footpaths: the zero line of a warped noise (scale 700), 8.4 units wide, swept paper with only a hair of grey where the track meets the grass; washes stop at the path

Decals, all drawn with the brush and gathered at features: broken dry strokes on the hard hill crests with clusters of moss dots, broken shore strokes snapped onto the bank, one or two ripple lines in open water (now and then a vermilion petal), reed stands on the banks, dry strokes along the path edges with a grass clump or pebble now and then, stepping stones where a path crosses water, loose grass clumps only where a meadow noise is high

characters.summary: Animals and one figure painted with a handful of strokes and baked once per pose. Main character: a wandering calligrapher (about 19 x 31 units, 38 up to the bristle tip) in a wide sedge hat with a pale-wash crown and a bold black brim, a bare-paper face in three-quarter profile, a pale grey robe held by one bold burnt-black back stroke, a vermilion sash knotted at the back whose two tails are painted live, straw-sandal dabs and a giant calligraphy brush strapped across the back. Small creature (two designs): a crow (about 22 x 14 units) with a wet black body, a dry-brush wing, a split beak and a bare-paper eye that hops; and a crab (about 27 x 17 units) of three wet dabs with jointed dry legs and raised claws. Fast creature: a pale carp (about 30 x 9 units) that swims through the air with a mist trail, a dark wet back, scale arcs and trailing barbels. Large creature: a tiger (about 49 x 29 units) with a pale granulated body, pressed stripes that wrap the volume, a ruff, angled brows over bare-paper eyes and a ringed S-shaped tail.
rules: Five to twelve strokes per part; every stroke has a pressed start and a tapering or dry end. Never close a contour completely.
Readability by value: crow and crab are the darkest masses, carp and tiger are pale washes held by black strokes, the main character carries the only vermilion; eyes and faces are bare paper.

Every pose is painted, not deformed: the main character has 4 idle poses (neutral, inhale, blink, look back), 8 walk poses (contact, down, passing, up per foot), 2 dash poses (crouched wind-up, lunge) and a hurt recoil; the crow has a 6-pose hop, the crab 4, the carp 6 swim poses, the tiger an 8-pose diagonal-pair gait.

Secondary motion: hat and brush lag the body, the sash tails hang and sway at rest, stream back when walking and fly flat in a dash; the tiger's head bobs a beat after the body and its tail swings with a growing lag; the carp's barbels and pectoral fin trail.
No lock-step crowds: each creature has its own tempo (0.9-1.1x) and size (0.93-1.07x) from its seed; the carp drifts on two slow unrelated swells.
Hit (0.14 s): knocked 1.4 units along the blow, tilted 0.17 rad, squashed to 116 % x 86 % with a squared falloff, and the ink is lifted to bare paper for the first half.

Death (0.35 s): five baked frames - the ink first pools wet and dark, then bleeds into the paper, pales and breaks up along the fibres while the body spreads 30 % and sinks 50 %; the carp rises 5 units and thins into mist.
Spawn (0.45 s): a drop of ink falls and spreads into a stain, a soft blurred blot wicks up out of it with an overshoot, then the crisp strokes are painted from the ground up (the carp tail first).

props.summary: Classic ink-painting motifs, each a few strokes, placed by the land rather than scattered: bamboo clumps (3-5 jointed stalks, 64-84 units tall) only in groves, plum trees with a gnarled dry trunk and vermilion blossoms leaning over the water, pines with S-curved trunks and needle wheels in twos and threes on the hill washes, rocks with a facet line and stacked axe-cut strokes by paths and shores (often with an orchid at the foot), a scholar rock with two waists and dark holes, rare misty mountains deep inside the hill washes, homesteads of a thatched hut with a stone lantern by the door and bamboo or a plum behind, lone lanterns where paths bend, reed stands on the banks and a fishing boat with a seated angler out on the ponds.
rules: Paint back to front: pale far parts (dan / qing) first, dark near parts on top; that value step is the only depth cue.
Every prop stands on a small feathered qing wash; trees, rocks, huts and lanterns add a soft shadow ellipse.
Clusters, not sprinkles: groves from a noise field, plums by the water, rocks and orchids together, a hut always comes with its lantern and a tree.
Vermilion only in plum blossoms and fallen petals.
Wind: bamboo, reeds, orchids and (less) plums and pines lean with a slow swell plus gusts that travel across the land - the top shears, the base stays; the boat rocks on the swell.
Tall props (mountains, pines, bamboo, plum) turn 45 % transparent when the main character walks behind them.

effects.name: Flung ink projectile
effects.how: A burnt-black drop (r 1.9) with a paper glint and a 21-unit tail that breaks into dry-brush bristle streaks, rotated along the flight; 40 % of throws shed a drop that falls and stays on the paper.

effects.name: Ink impact
effects.how: Layered: a 0.12 s ink flick at the point of contact (8-12 units), a 0.32 s directional splatter sprite thrown along the blow (pressed blot, tapered streaks, end drops), three drops flung forward that land and stay up to 1.3 s; a pale puff for the carp.

effects.name: Ink burst
effects.how: A 0.3 s splash (17 / 32 units), a directional splatter, 9-18 drops of which 75 % leave in a fan along the last blow with big drops falling short and small ones flying far, then a bleed bloom on the paper: a pale uneven stain with a darker tide line and two or three backrun lobes that spreads fast, holds and soaks away over 1.1-1.6 s. Crows also shed four rocking feathers; carps thin into three mist puffs.

effects.name: Orbiting ensō
effects.how: Small one-stroke circles (r 5.6, 1.7 units wide, pressed start, dry end, open gap) with a vermilion dot, a pale shadow and a dry-brush wake: two thin tapering dan ribbons that follow the circle's real path over the last 0.2 s.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small: a burnt-black ink bead (teardrop 5 x 8 units) with a paper glint. Large: a vermilion square seal (9.6 units) with eroded edges and carved abstract strokes that bobs and tilts. Collecting a seal stamps it onto the paper (it comes down at 145 % and settles in 0.11 s, then soaks in) and lifts five petals.

effects.name: Ensō glow-up
effects.how: A large one-stroke circle (r 14, 2.5 units wide) painted in one movement around the main character (sweep to 330 degrees in 0.54 s) with the loaded brush head as a dot at the front, five drops jumping from the start point, twelve vermilion petals scattering; it fades into the paper over 1.4 s.

effects.name: Dash
effects.how: A crouched wind-up pose for 50 ms, then the lunge with two pale-ink after-images 7 units apart (20 / 10 %), a 30-unit dry streak in dan and four drops left on the ground.

effects.name: Floating numbers
effects.how: Ma Shan Zheng numerals, 10 units, black ink with a paper outline; accented ones 13 units in paper colour on a small vermilion seal; pop 0.55 -> 1.15 -> 1 with a slight tilt.

atmosphere.summary: The screen is a painting with an unpainted margin: the edges fade into misty paper along a fibre-feathered border, slow bands of mist drift across the world, rings open now and then on the water, and the lower left carries a column of abstract calligraphy with a square and a round vermilion seal. Hurt makes black ink seep in from the margin.
rules: Margin: a rounded rectangle (radius 10 % of the height) whose outside fades to paper #f3ecdd at up to 82 % over 11 % of the height, edge displaced by wash noise and fibres; built once per screen size, drawn as four strips.

Mist bands: three in eight 460 x 230-unit cells carry a soft paper-coloured band 240-380 units wide that drifts 5-11 units/s with alpha 0.32 sin(pi * phase), so it fades in and out instead of popping.
Water life: in 60 % of 80-unit cells inside water a pair of rings opens every 3.6-6.2 s (radius 1.5 -> 11 units, ease-out, 0.8 s apart) and fades.
Inscription: four abstract glyphs 3.4 % of the height tall in nong at 72 %, a square seal with carved strokes and a small round seal below - never real script.
Hurt: ink #2c2926 seeps in from the margin along noise, up to 62 % alpha, fading with the hurt timer.
No vignette darkening, no glow, no colour grading: the paper itself is the light.

ui.summary: Mounted scrolls and brush strokes. Cards are hanging scrolls: a cord and hook, a dark rod, grey silk mounting with a faint diagonal weave, pale strips, a paper field with fibres and a heavy bottom roller with knobs; the clock plaque and the caption bar are small handscrolls with dark rollers at both ends. Bars are single brush strokes (pale dry track, black ink fill with a ragged dry-brush end). Counters and numbers are Ma Shan Zheng ink; the counter icon is the crow itself, painted with the same strokes; vermilion seals mark the level box, card keys and titles. Titles sit on one broad pale wash stroke.

motion: Hand-painted timing on twos: the main character's walk shows 8 poses at 12 fps (frame = distance * 0.13, one stride pair per 0.67 s at walking speed) with a body drop of +0.75 on the down pose and -0.55 on the up pose; idle runs on a 12 fps clock - inhale and hold every 1.25 s, blinks on two unrelated clocks (3.9 s and 5.1 s), a look back for 1.7 s every 12.6 s.

Creatures advance their poses by distance travelled, each on its own tempo: crow hop (6 poses: crouch, push-off, rise, downstroke, land, settle) at about 9 fps, crab 4 poses, carp 6 swim poses at about 9 fps, tiger 8 poses at about 8 fps.

Anticipation and follow-through: the crow crouches before each hop and lands tail-up; the dash starts with a crouched wind-up; hat, brush, sash tails, the tiger's head and tail and the carp's barbels lag behind.
Spawn 0.45 s (drop, stain, soft blot with outBack overshoot, strokes painted upward); hit 0.14 s (knock-back, squash, paper flash); death 0.35 s in five frames (pool, bleed, break up).

Effects ease out: splashes 0.12-0.3 s, splatters 0.32-0.45 s, landed drops 1-1.8 s, blooms spread with outQuad and hold before soaking away (1.1-1.6 s), feathers rock down over 1.3-1.8 s, petals 0.8-1.5 s with a sideways flutter.
Ambient motion is slower than the actors: plants shear in travelling gusts (0.7 and 1.9 rad/s), mist bands drift 5-11 units/s, rings open on the water every few seconds, the boat rocks at 1.1 rad/s.
do: Paint every shape with a few confident strokes: pressed start, tapering or dry end, never a uniform line.
Draw each animation pose as its own painting (contact, down, passing, up; crouch, push-off, land) and keep strokes seeded per part so they do not boil.
Leave most of the sheet empty; let water, faces, eyes and bellies be bare paper.
Gather marks at features: crest strokes on the hard edge of a wash, reeds on banks, rocks by paths, a lantern by every hut.
Use the five ink tones for depth: pale far, dark near; far legs and wings one tone paler.
Give effects a direction and a life cycle: flick, splatter along the blow, drops that land and stay, a bloom that soaks away.
Keep vermilion for seals, blossoms and the main character's sash; one accent only.
dont: Don't add a second colour, colour-tinted water or coloured shadows.
Don't outline shapes with closed constant-width lines; that turns ink into a cartoon.
Don't sprinkle tufts or dots evenly over the ground; clutter destroys the empty space.
Don't animate by squashing one drawing; paint the poses and add lag on hat, sash, tail and brush.
Don't use hard flat colour blocks or crisp vector edges; washes always feather into the paper.
Don't use pure white or pure black.
Don't write legible text in seals or inscriptions; use abstract glyph strokes.
performance: Init bakes about 115 sprites (39 character poses - 15 main character, 6 crow, 4 crab, 6 carp, 8 tiger - each with a mirrored and a paper-flash copy, 4 blurred spawn copies, 20 death frames, 21 prop variants, ~30 effect sprites and the HUD textures) in about 1.5 s: textures 0.25 s, characters 0.8 s, props 0.28 s, effects and HUD 0.2 s; the blurred blots and bleed halos of the washes are the main cost. Ground chunks (256 units, up to 640 px) are built by a generator in 5 ms slices: fields on a 16 px grid, a per-pixel loop that only reads textures and interpolates, then decals. Per frame everything is drawImage of baked canvases plus two live paths per sash and per orbit wake; frame cost stays within about 5 % of the previous version of the module measured the same way.
